quizzes.subject: Akhlaq
quizzes.title: Akhlaq Mastery: Truthfulness, Trust & Everyday Integrity
quizzes.description: Test your understanding of core ethical virtues (Sidq, Amanah), honesty with parents, and keeping promises in school life.

questions.question: What is the Islamic term for absolute honesty in speech and conviction?
options: Amanah (Trustworthiness)
Sidq (Truthfulness)
Sabr (Patience)
Shukr (Gratitude)
questions.explanation: Sidq denotes truthfulness in words, actions, and internal intentions, regarded as a cornerstone of prophetic character.

questions.question: When a classmate entrusts you with personal stationery or confidential study notes, which moral duty are you upholding?
options: Hilm (Gentleness)
Amanah (Custodianship of Trust)
Zuhd (Asceticism)
Tawakkul (Reliance)
questions.explanation: Amanah means preserving whatever trusts or responsibilities have been placed in your care without betrayal or misuse.

questions.question: According to prophetic teachings, how should a believer respond when treated harshly or insulted by another person?
options: Retaliate with double the harshness
Respond with patience (Sabr) and dignified calm words
Boycott the entire community permanently
Pretend nothing happened while holding resentment
questions.explanation: Restraint and meeting harshness with gracious composure (Ihsan and Sabr) extinguishes animosity and builds nobility.

questions.question: What is the primary spiritual reason for removing harmful objects (e.g., glass, stones, thorns) from a public pathway?
options: To gain recognition from school prefects
It is recognized as a branch of Faith (Iman) and charity (Sadaqah)
To satisfy municipal regulations
To avoid physical exercise
questions.explanation: The Prophet (PBUH) stated that removing harm from the path is among the branches of faith and counts as an act of charity.

questions.question: Which of the following describes Birr al-Walidayn (Devotion to Parents)?
options: Obeying them only when their requests match your personal hobbies
Speaking to them with honor, gentle tone, and serving their needs with empathy
Ignoring them during disagreements
Communicating with them only through text messages
questions.explanation: Birr al-Walidayn is a supreme duty commanding honor, humility, gentle speech, and continuous care for mother and father.

quizzes.subject: Akhlaq
quizzes.title: Akhlaq & Social Responsibility: Rights of Neighbors & Digital Etiquette
quizzes.description: Explore ethics regarding neighbors, community rights, speech discipline, and avoiding slander on digital networks.

questions.question: What is the ruling regarding the privacy of neighbors and peers in Islamic social ethics?
options: Peeking into private properties is permitted if curious
Tajassus (spying/snooping into private affairs) is strictly forbidden
Privacy only applies during nighttime hours
Neighbors have no expectation of privacy in neighborhoods
questions.explanation: The Quran explicitly commands: "Do not spy on one another" (Surah Al-Hujurat 49:12), protecting personal sanctuary.

questions.question: What is Ghibah (Backbiting) as defined by the Prophet (PBUH)?
options: Speaking ill of someone in their presence
Mentioning something about your brother/sister in their absence that they would dislike
Reporting a factual emergency to authorities
Complimenting someone publicly
questions.explanation: Ghibah is mentioning a fellow human behind their back with attributes or statements they would be displeased with.

questions.question: When using social media or group messaging, what responsibility does a student bear before forwarding information?
options: Forward it immediately if it sounds dramatic
Tabayyun - rigorously verify authenticity and purpose before sharing
Share without checking as long as others shared it
Add personal exaggerations to increase engagement
questions.explanation: The principle of Tabayyun (investigation/verification) is mandatory to prevent circulating falsehoods and discord.

quizzes.subject: Fiqh
quizzes.title: Fiqh Essentials: Taharah (Purification) & Wudu Regulations
quizzes.description: Master the prerequisites of purity, valid water classifications, obligatory acts of ablution (Faraid of Wudu), and its nullifiers.

questions.question: How many obligatory actions (Faraid) of Wudu are explicitly derived from Surah Al-Ma’idah (5:6)?
options: Three
Four
Six
Eight
questions.explanation: The 4 canonical Faraid of Wudu are: washing face, washing arms including elbows, wiping head, and washing feet including ankles.

questions.question: Which type of water is classified as "Tahur" (pure and purifying) suitable for lifting ritual impurity?
options: Water whose color and taste have permanently changed with cooking broth
Natural rainwater, well water, river, or sea water in its original condition
Water mixed with chemical dye
Used water that touched ritual contaminants
questions.explanation: Al-Ma’ al-Mutlaq (natural unconditional water like rain, snow, sea, or spring water) retains both purity and purifying power.

questions.question: Which of the following invalidates (nullifies) Wudu?
options: Reciting the Holy Quran from memory
Falling into deep sleep where consciousness of surroundings is lost
Drinking cold fresh water
Clipping fingernails during daytime
questions.explanation: Deep slumber wherein one loses consciousness is a nullifier of Wudu as one cannot be certain of maintaining purity.

questions.question: What is Tayammum in Islamic jurisprudence?
options: A substitute dry ablution using clean earth/soil when water is unavailable or medically harmful
A special prayer recited after sunset
Washing only the feet without the face
A ritual meal eaten before dawn
questions.explanation: Tayammum provides a divine dispensation using clean earth when water cannot be procured or poses verified physical injury.

questions.question: What is the condition of clothes (Thawb) required for valid Salat performance?
options: Must be made of imported silk for men
Must be clean and free from physical impurities (Najasah) and cover the Awrah
Must be brand new from a boutique
Must have three distinct layers
questions.explanation: Salat requires Taharat ath-Thawb (cleanliness of garments free from Najasah) and proper coverage of the prescribed Awrah.

quizzes.subject: Fiqh
quizzes.title: Fiqh of Salat: Pillars, Conditions & Congregational Rules
quizzes.description: Differentiate between Shurut (conditions) and Arkan (pillars) of daily prayers, Sujud Sahw, and traveler dispensations.

questions.question: What is the critical difference between a Shart (condition) and a Rukn (pillar) of Salat?
options: There is no difference; they are exact synonyms
A Shart must precede and remain throughout the prayer (e.g. Qiblah), whereas a Rukn is an integral internal action (e.g. Ruku)
A Shart is optional while a Rukn is forbidden
A Rukn can be substituted with money but a Shart cannot
questions.explanation: Conditions (Shurut) exist outside/before the act (like Wudu and Qiblah facing), while Pillars (Arkan) constitute its internal core.

questions.question: If a worshipper in prayer unintentionally misses a Sunnah Mu’akkadah act or doubts the number of Rak’ahs, what rectifies the error?
options: Abandoning the prayer and re-performing Wudu
Performing Sujud as-Sahw (Prostrations of Forgetfulness)
Paying immediate charity to a fellow worshipper
Repeating the entire prayer three times
questions.explanation: Sujud as-Sahw is legislated by prophetic guidance to rectify omissions, doubts, or unintended minor additions in Salat.

questions.question: What is the ruling for Qasr (shortening prayers) during legitimate travel?
options: 4-Rak’ah obligatory prayers (Dhuhr, Asr, Isha) are shortened to 2 Rak’ahs
All prayers including Maghrib and Fajr are reduced to 1 Rak’ah
Travelers are completely exempt from praying until returning home
Only Friday prayer can be shortened
questions.explanation: Under traveler concessions (Rukhsah), the 4-Rak’ah Fard prayers are shortened to 2 Rak’ahs, while Maghrib (3) and Fajr (2) remain unchanged.

quizzes.subject: Seerah
quizzes.title: Seerah Chronology: Life in Makkah & The First Revelation
quizzes.description: Trace the lineage of the Prophet (PBUH), the year of the Elephant, the Cave of Hira, and the early callers to Islam.

questions.question: Before receiving revelation, by which honorable titles was Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) universally known in Makkah?
options: Al-Amin (The Trustworthy) and As-Sadiq (The Truthful)
Al-Hakim and Al-Qadi
Al-Fatih and Al-Mansur
The King of Quraysh
questions.explanation: Even before prophethood, his unimpeachable honesty led the Quraysh citizens to address him as As-Sadiq and Al-Amin.

questions.question: In which cave near Makkah did the Prophet (PBUH) engage in contemplative worship (Tahannuth) when revelation first descended?
options: Cave of Thawr
Cave of Hira on Jabal an-Nur
Cave of Uhud
Cave of Kahf
questions.explanation: Archangel Jibril (Gabriel) appeared to the Prophet in the Cave of Hira located on Jabal an-Nur (Mount of Light).

questions.question: Which were the first five verses of the Holy Quran revealed to humanity?
options: Surah Al-Fatihah (1:1-5)
Surah Al-Alaq (96:1-5) beginning with "Iqra' bismi Rabbika alladhi khalaq"
Surah Al-Baqarah (2:1-5)
Surah Al-Ikhlas (112:1-4)
questions.explanation: "Read! In the Name of your Lord Who created..." from Surah Al-Alaq constituted the dawn of divine revelation.

questions.question: Who was the first adult female to believe in the Prophet’s message and console him after the first revelation?
options: Aisha bint Abi Bakr
Khadijah bint Khuwaylid (RA)
Fatimah az-Zahra
Hafsah bint Umar
questions.explanation: His noble wife Khadijah (RA) immediately believed in his prophethood, offering unwavering emotional and material support.

questions.question: Where did the early persecuted Muslims seek refuge during the first emigration (Hijrah) sanctioned by the Prophet?
options: Yemen
Abyssinia (Al-Habasha / Ethiopia) under King Negus (An-Najashi)
Constantinople
Damascus
questions.explanation: The Prophet sent companions to Abyssinia, praising its Christian king An-Najashi as a ruler under whom no one was wronged.

quizzes.subject: Seerah
quizzes.title: Seerah in Madinah: The Constitution & Treaty of Hudaybiyyah
quizzes.description: Analyze state-building in Madinah, the fraternal bond between Muhajirun and Ansar, and diplomatic triumphs.

questions.question: What was the foundational document established by the Prophet upon arriving in Madinah guaranteeing rights to all communities?
options: The Charter of Medina (Sahifat al-Madinah)
The Code of Hammurabi
The Treaty of Rome
The Edict of Yathrib
questions.explanation: Sahifat al-Madinah established civic rights, joint defense, freedom of conscience, and rule of law across diverse communities.

questions.question: Why did the Quran characterize the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah as a "Manifest Victory" (Fathan Mubeena)?
options: Because large amounts of gold were captured
It ended armed hostilities, created diplomatic recognition, and allowed peaceful dialogue that multiplied the community
It allowed immediate entry into Roman trade routes
It resulted in instant military surrender of enemies
questions.explanation: Peace allowed uninterrupted intellectual exchange, leading more people to accept the faith in two years than in the previous twenty.

questions.question: During the Conquest of Makkah (Fath Makkah), how did the Prophet (PBUH) treat those who had persecuted Muslims for two decades?
options: He ordered general imprisonment of all leaders
He issued a general amnesty declaring: "Go, for you are the free ones" (Idh-habu fa-antum at-tulaqa')
He demanded all wealth be surrendered
He dismantled the civilian dwellings
questions.explanation: In a historic demonstration of mercy, the Prophet granted general amnesty without revenge, echoing Prophet Yusuf’s words.
